prompt: Create a high-fidelity desktop landing-page UI mockup for BugReceipt, a privacy-first Chrome extension that records a tab, console errors, network activity, and manual QA steps, then lets the user review and export evidence locally. Use the two reference images only for BugReceipt's established visual identity and the real extension interface; do not copy the old page structure and do not use the name ReproKit. Canvas 1536x1024, polished product-design screenshot, credible browser-product marketing page. Direction: TRIAGE DESK. Keep the established colors exactly in spirit: deep ink navy, pale paper/fog blue, thin desaturated blue rules, coral signal accent, teal trace accent. Square geometry, thin technical rules, Bricolage-Grotesque-like display type and compact monospaced labels. Make the first viewport feel like a live QA triage desk while retaining a clear persuasive marketing hierarchy. Use a compact top navigation and headline band with the statement "One capture. The whole failure." and a primary CTA "Download BugReceipt". Under it, create one asymmetric connected work surface, not a collection of floating cards: a narrow issue summary column on the left, a large central extension workflow showing active tab recording and review, and a narrow export receipt column on the right listing video.webm, console.json, network.json, and report.md. Connect the three zones with thin trace rules and numbered annotations. Include an ink-dark evidence region behind part of the product UI and a coral recording timer/status strip. Add the privacy boundary "Evidence stays local until export." The product interface must remain the dominant object and the page must still read immediately as a landing page, not an admin dashboard. No rounded card grid, no bento layout, no gradients, no glassmorphism, no decorative blobs, no fake testimonials, no pill-heavy UI. All text must be crisp and correctly spelled.
decision: Superseded by the user's corrected Failure Trace Timeline selection.
